newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Wednesday but remained at high levels supported by new A share listings on Shanghai and Shenzhen this week, traders said.
The most active three-day contract fell slightly to 24.80 percent from 25.00 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover fell to 5.42 million lots from 11.29 million on Tuesday. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said falls in turnover were due to a pause in new A share issues over the rest of the week.
But today's three A share listings and five new listings over the next two days prevented the rates from falling sharply.
"If new issues and listings continue on the A share markets in the mid-term, the rates will stay at high levels," a trader said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up after a technical correction and further rises were likely in the next few days, traders said.
Combined volume on the nine-contract market rose slightly to 1.43 million lots from 1.20 million on Tuesday.
The most active three-year bond that matures on August 1999, bucked the trend to close at 104.10 yuan, down from Tuesday's 104.17 yuan on turnover of 684 million yuan.
Traders said the bond opened higher but profit-taking pushed it down late in the session.
"The spots are likely to rise further in the next few days after profit-taking is digested tomorrow," one trader said.
Expectations of cuts in both bank interest rates and bank reserve ratios would be an important factor supporting the spots in the mid-term, traders said.
